To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have designed a workflow for the dynamic management of lexical resources; we have developed a web application framework to support the workflow; and we have tested it with a real use case.

we designed a web application framework for the management of dynamic computational lexicons, where lexicons interact by reciprocating semantic information, and that we have implemented the framework in the context of the Italian language.
1) LeXFlow is a framework for the dynamic management of lexical resources, 2) the framework is based on the notion of lexical flow (LF), and 3) the LFs can be implemented as web applications.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new generation of lexicons that can be automatically updated and that can be used as a source for the enrichment of other lexicons.
the design of a framework for managing the evolution of lexicons, and the development of a prototype of a web application that implements the lexical flow.
the design of a framework where the dynamic enrichment of lexicons can be carried out by the interaction of different agents, including humans, automatic applications and other lexicons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
LeXFlow is an innovative framework that allows for the dynamic creation of computational lexicons by means of lexical flows.
LeXFlow is an application framework where lexicon management is modelled as a workflow instance and where lexicons are enriched by means of a lexical flow.
the lexical flow allows for the creation of new lexicon entries, which can be further enriched by means of the flow, thus creating a dynamic lexicon.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a web application framework for the management of dynamic multi-source computational lexicons, and we have implemented a prototype of this framework, LeXFlow, which we have tested on two different lexicons.
we are moving from static to dynamic lexicons and from single-source to multi-source lexicons.

LeXFlow allows to: (i) manage lexicons in a dynamic way, where the information of one lexicon is automatically propagated to the others, and (ii) to automatically enrich lexicons with new semantic relations, by means of a corpus-based application.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the adoption of standards is not only beneficial for the interoperability of lexical resources, but also for fostering the creation and management of dynamic lexicons.
, by adopting a workflow-like perspective, it is possible to model lexicon management as an activity which can be automated and, thus, be more efficient, and at the same time, more effective.
LeXFlow is a flexible framework that can be used in a number of scenarios, ranging from the management of dynamic multi-source lexical resources, to the development of new lexicons.
